basics.description: **Abstract Security for Microsoft Sentinel: one-deploy solution** Abstract Security: a security data pipeline and agentic SIEM in one platform. One Azure deployment that creates the Data Collection Endpoint, Data Collection Rule and tables that Abstract Security sends events to through the Logs Ingestion API, and installs Microsoft Sentinel content for that data. **Abstract Security for Microsoft Sentinel** sets up, in one deployment, everything Abstract needs to deliver data into Microsoft Sentinel. Choose the resource group that holds your Sentinel workspace, or a new one. Every field below explains what it sets, when to change it and what follows.

location.label: Region
location.toolTip: What: the region of a new workspace and of the Data Collection Endpoint and Rule. With an existing workspace, the endpoint and rule follow the workspace's region whatever is chosen here.

options.text: Pick what to set up below, and the form shows only the tabs and fields that choice needs. The full set is the Log Analytics workspace (new or yours), the Data Collection Endpoint and Rule Abstract sends to, the AbstractEventLogs_CL table, optional routes into the Microsoft ASIM tables, a data-lake table and vendor tables, the Abstract content (data connector page, parser, analytics rules, hunting queries, workbooks, playbooks and automation rules) and the read-only discovery inventory. Have ready: Contributor and User Access Administrator (or Owner) on the resource group, and the Abstract app registration if Abstract has already given you one.

This wizard sets up: Content only. Installs the Abstract content into a workspace that already has the data plane from an earlier deployment: the data connector page, the ASim_AbstractEvent parser, analytics rules (installed disabled), hunting queries, workbooks, playbooks and automation rules.

basics.name: depth
basics.label: How much to show
basics.toolTip: What: 'Recommended settings' shows only what a first install needs and uses Abstract's defaults for the rest; 'Show every setting' shows every option (retention, table plans, individual content switches, discovery tuning). When: keep the recommended view unless you have a reason to tune. Consequence: a hidden setting always sends its default, so switching back never deploys a value you set by mistake. Portal: every setting is also described in the template's README.

body.query: [concat('resources | where subscriptionId =~ "', subscription().subscriptionId, '" and type =~ "microsoft.operationalinsights/workspaces" and resourceGroup =~ "', resourceGroup().name, '" | project name, location, id = tolower(id), retention = toint(properties.retentionInDays), sku = tostring(properties.sku.name) | join kind=leftouter (resources | where type =~ "microsoft.operationsmanagement/solutions" and name startswith "SecurityInsights(" | project id = tolower(tostring(properties.workspaceResourceId)), hasSentinel = 1) on id | extend sentinel = iff(isnotnull(hasSentinel), "yes", "no") | project name, location, retention, sku, sentinel | order by name asc')]

basics.name: workspaceMode
basics.label: Log Analytics workspace
basics.toolTip: What: the Microsoft Sentinel workspace Abstract writes to. When: choose 'Create new' for a fresh workspace with Microsoft Sentinel switched on; choose 'Use existing' to add Abstract to a workspace that already runs Microsoft Sentinel. Consequence: an existing workspace is never modified (its retention, pricing tier and other tables are left alone). It must be in the resource group chosen above. Find yours: Azure portal > Microsoft Sentinel > the workspace > Overview > Resource group.

basics.name: workspaceNameNew
basics.label: New workspace name
basics.toolTip: What: the name of the new Log Analytics workspace. When: leave empty and the deployment names it abstract-sentinel-<unique suffix>. Consequence: the name cannot be changed later. 4 to 63 letters, digits and hyphens. The form checks it against the workspaces already in this resource group.

validations.message: 4 to 63 letters, digits and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit.
A workspace with this name is already in this resource group. Choose 'Use existing' instead, or pick another name: creating it again would update that workspace.

basics.name: workspaceRetentionDays
basics.label: Retention of the new workspace
basics.toolTip: What: how long the new workspace keeps data in its interactive (Analytics) tier. When: 90 days is included in the Microsoft Sentinel price; longer costs per GB per month. Consequence: applies to the new workspace only; change it later in Log Analytics workspace > Usage and estimated costs > Data retention.

elements.name: deployDataConnectors
elements.label: Data connector tile
elements.toolTip: What: the 'Abstract Security (Security Data Pipeline)' tile in Microsoft Sentinel > Data connectors. Its status reads AbstractEventLogs_CL and Abstract rows in the ASim tables. Consequence: none on data; it only shows whether data is arriving. When: keep on unless you do not want the tile.

elements.name: deployParsers
elements.label: ASim_AbstractEvent parser
elements.toolTip: What: a workspace function that presents AbstractEventLogs_CL in ASIM shape. The hunting queries use it. Consequence: without it the hunting queries fail. Portal: Log Analytics workspace > Logs > Functions. When: keep on if you use the hunting queries.

elements.name: deployAnalyticsRules
elements.label: Analytics rules (3)
elements.toolTip: What: 'Abstract Security - High or Critical event', 'Abstract - Repeated auth failures followed by success' and 'Abstract Security - Finding' (findings from the asim-alert lane). They read AbstractEventLogs_CL and the ASim tables directly. Consequence: none until you turn one on below. When: keep on. Portal: Microsoft Sentinel > Analytics.

elements.name: enabledAnalyticsRules
elements.label: Turn these rules on
elements.toolTip: What: the analytics rules that run. Each runs every hour and can create incidents. When: choose Abstract finding if Abstract findings reach Sentinel (the asim-alert vendor table), and the High or critical rule only if findings do not, or the same event raises two incidents. Consequence: a rule left out is installed but off. Portal: Microsoft Sentinel > Analytics.

allowedValues.label: Abstract finding: one incident per Abstract finding
Repeated sign-in failures followed by a success

elements.name: deployHuntingQueries
elements.label: Hunting queries (3)
elements.toolTip: What: 'Rare or newly-seen product', 'High cumulative-risk identities' and 'Daily value & reduction summary'. Portal: Microsoft Sentinel > Hunting > Queries. When: keep on. Consequence: none on data; queries run only when someone opens them.

elements.name: deployWorkbooks
elements.label: Workbooks: Pipeline Overview, Value & ROI
elements.toolTip: What: two workbooks on Abstract's pipeline volume, reduction and cost. Portal: Microsoft Sentinel > Workbooks > My workbooks. When: keep on. Consequence: none on data; opened on demand.

elements.name: deployDiscoveryWorkbook
elements.label: Workbook: Sentinel Discovery
elements.toolTip: What: a workbook that inventories the workspace's tables, connectors and ingestion so you can see what Abstract could take over. Portal: Microsoft Sentinel > Workbooks > My workbooks. When: keep on. Consequence: none on data; opened on demand.

elements.name: deployAutomationRules
elements.label: Automation rule: tag and prioritise Abstract incidents
elements.toolTip: What: labels incidents raised by this solution's rules. Consequence: none until it is turned on below. When: keep on. Portal: Microsoft Sentinel > Automation.

elements.name: enableAutomationRules
elements.label: Turn the automation rules on
elements.toolTip: What: turns on the tag-and-prioritise rule and, when the Playbooks tab installs them, the rules that run Verdict and Tune at source. Consequence: they act on new incidents from this solution's rules. When: turn on once you have read what each rule does. Portal: Microsoft Sentinel > Automation.

elements.name: on_existingDataPlane
elements.label: Your existing data plane

options.text: This deployment installs the content without the data plane. The ASim_AbstractEvent parser it installs reads exactly the tables the existing data plane stores events in, so it needs four settings of the deployment that built that data plane: ASIM tables, store-once, vendor tables and vendor events kept out of ASIM. Pick that deployment's Data Collection Rule and the form reads them from it. Nothing in the data plane changes.

body.query: [concat('resources | where subscriptionId =~ "', subscription().subscriptionId, '" and resourceGroup =~ "', resourceGroup().name, '" and type =~ "microsoft.insights/datacollectionrules" and isnotnull(properties.streamDeclarations["Custom-AbstractEventLogs_CL"]) | project name, location | order by name asc')]

elements.name: dpRule
elements.label: Data Collection Rule of the existing data plane
elements.toolTip: What: the Abstract Data Collection Rules in this resource group (rules that declare Custom-AbstractEventLogs_CL), read live from Azure Resource Graph. When: pick the rule the earlier deployment created (abstract-dcr unless it was renamed). Consequence: the form reads the rule's dataflows and sends the ASIM, store-once and vendor settings they show, so the parser reads the same tables; pick the last entry to answer the questions yourself. Portal: Monitor > Settings > Data Collection Rules.
